boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten distinct, university-documented study environments on Detroit Mercy’s McNichols Campus.

cards.title: McNichols Campus Library Stacks
cards.subtitle: McNichols Campus Library
cards.notes: Bring a book or laptop and work among the library collections; the university’s study-space guide specifically lists the stacks for informal use.
cards.short_summary: A collection-side setting for individual reading and research.
cards.evidence_claim: Detroit Mercy’s student meeting/study-spaces guide lists the Library “Stacks and Quiet study rooms” as informally used indoor space.
cards.access_notes: Use during library access hours; confirm current hours with the library before visiting.

cards.title: McNichols Campus Library Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: McNichols Campus Library
cards.notes: Use one of the six library study rooms when you need a defined work setting; check with library staff for current room-use procedures.
cards.short_summary: Six dedicated study rooms in the campus library.
cards.evidence_claim: Detroit Mercy’s study-space guide identifies “(6) Library Study Rooms” as formally reserved indoor student space.
cards.access_notes: Formally reserved space; verify reservation requirements and library hours before planning a session.

cards.title: Quad Commons Lounge
cards.subtitle: Quad Commons, first floor
cards.notes: Set up at the soft seating or laptop bar in the first-floor lounge; treat it as a residential-area space and respect community access rules.
cards.short_summary: A lounge with soft seating and a laptop bar.
cards.evidence_claim: Detroit Mercy lists the Quad Commons first-floor lounge, with soft seating and a laptop bar, as a formally reserved indoor study space.
cards.access_notes: Located in a residential area; confirm resident or event access with Residence Life.

cards.title: Holden Hall Fireplace Lounge
cards.subtitle: Holden Hall, first floor
cards.notes: Use the first-floor fireplace lounge for a change of setting, keeping in mind that it sits in a residence hall and access may be limited.
cards.short_summary: A first-floor residence-hall lounge centered on a fireplace.
cards.evidence_claim: Detroit Mercy’s guide lists the “Holden Hall 1st floor—Fireplace Lounge” as informally used indoor study space.
cards.access_notes: Residential-area location; check Residence Life access expectations before going.

cards.entity_name: Student Union Student Study Rooms 57, 58 and 59
cards.title: Student Union Study Rooms 57, 58 & 59
cards.subtitle: Student Union
cards.notes: Choose rooms 57, 58, or 59 when a designated study room fits the task; ask Student Life about current scheduling or access details.
cards.short_summary: Three numbered study rooms in the Student Union.
cards.evidence_claim: Detroit Mercy identifies Student Union Student Study Rooms 57, 58 and 59 as formally reserved indoor study spaces.
cards.access_notes: Formally reserved; confirm room availability and reservation process with Student Life.

cards.title: Fountain Lounge
cards.subtitle: Student Union, first floor
cards.notes: Work from the first-floor Student Union lounge, then take a short reset by the windows facing Fisher Fountain if your work benefits from daylight.
cards.short_summary: A window-facing Student Union lounge by Fisher Fountain.
cards.evidence_claim: Detroit Mercy’s style guide places Fountain Lounge on the first floor of the Student Union and notes its windows face Fisher Fountain; its study guide lists it for informal indoor use.
cards.source_title: Building, location and special room names
cards.access_notes: Informally used space in the Student Union; follow posted building access rules.

cards.title: The Loft Dining Area
cards.subtitle: Student Union, second floor
cards.notes: Use the dining area between classes when you need an informal campus table; keep the space available for diners and follow dining-area policies.
cards.short_summary: An informal work setting in the Student Union’s Loft.
cards.evidence_claim: Detroit Mercy’s student study-space guide lists the Loft Dining Area as an informally used indoor space.
cards.access_notes: Informal dining-area space; access and seating can be affected by dining operations.

cards.title: Architecture Pit
cards.subtitle: Warren Loranger Architecture Building
cards.notes: Use the Architecture Pit as an informal indoor work stop, especially for a short individual session; remain mindful of classes and building activity.
cards.short_summary: An informal study location inside the architecture building.
cards.evidence_claim: Detroit Mercy’s student meeting/study-spaces guide lists the Architecture Pit as an informally used indoor study space.
cards.access_notes: Informal space; follow building access rules and avoid disrupting scheduled instruction.

cards.title: Commerce & Finance Lower Level Lounge
cards.subtitle: Commerce & Finance Building, lower level
cards.notes: Head to the lower-level lounge for an informal indoor session; bring what you need and leave the shared space ready for the next visitor.
cards.short_summary: A lower-level lounge in the Commerce & Finance Building.
cards.evidence_claim: Detroit Mercy’s guide lists the Commerce & Finance LL Lounge as an informally used indoor study space.
cards.access_notes: Informal space; follow current Commerce & Finance Building access rules.

cards.title: CHP Study Room 131
cards.subtitle: College of Health Professions, Room 131
cards.notes: Use this designated room when its formal reservation status matches your plans; verify availability with the College of Health Professions before arriving.
cards.short_summary: A designated study room in the College of Health Professions.
cards.evidence_claim: Detroit Mercy’s student meeting/study-spaces guide lists CHP Study Room 131 as a formally reserved indoor study space.
cards.access_notes: Formally reserved; confirm room access and reservation requirements with the College of Health Professions.
